messages:
Alice Chen: Heads up — after opt-in migration of ~25 tenants to v2 we observed billing deltas. acme-prod saw ~+18% billed tokens for identical prompt sets. Noticed this on gpt-open-1 and rtx-8 runs. Likely tokenization differences (v2 uses different tokenizer variant) and seqlen distribution effects. Need quick plan for customers hitting unexpected quota/billing spikes.
Ben Rao: Oof. Short term idea: introduce a per-tenant billing normalization factor so legacy billing stays stable. Compute a billing_equiv_tokens value derived from raw tokens, store both raw and equiv, and surface equiv in console.
Carla Mendez: +1 on surfacing, but caution: normalizing billing can hide actual compute costs. v2 sometimes does less compute per token for longer contexts; if we bill by legacy tokens we'll undercharge ops. We should keep both metrics and ensure finance sees real compute usage.
Dana Ortiz: Proposal: keep three numbers in usage records: raw_tokens_v2, estimated_legacy_tokens (derived), and billing_tokens. Console should show raw vs legacy comparison and an explanatory tooltip. Offer an opt-in window (e.g., 90 days) where tenant can choose legacy-equivalent billing during migration.
Ben Rao: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```python
def compute_billing_tokens(tenant, model, raw_tokens, seq_len):
    if tenant.flags.get('billing_equiv'):
        factor = tenant.billing_equiv_factor(model, seq_len_bucket(seq_len))
        return int(raw_tokens * factor)
    return raw_tokens
```
Add header option for upstream callers if we want to force legacy accounting for troubleshooting: `X-Billing-Mode: legacy-equivalent`.
Carla Mendez: Where do we get `billing_equiv_factor`? We need a telemetry job to compute median `raw_v2 / raw_v1` ratio per model and seq-len bucket. Factors should be per-model and bucketed by seqlen (0-128,129-512,513-1024,>1024).
Alice Chen: I ran a quick adhoc query across migrated tenants: for `gpt-open-1`, seqlen < 128 ratio ≈ 1.15, 128-512 ≈ 1.08, >1024 ≈ 0.98. So a single-factor is insufficient — must bucket.
Dana Ortiz: UX questions: show both counts side-by-side, and a banner on tenant console when their predicted monthly bill changes >5%. Legal/finance prefer one-time credit over changing invoice math retroactively. Ops: credits are painful but maybe simpler than rewriting billing pipeline quickly.
Ben Rao: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) Add 'predicted billing delta' to console for any tenant switching to v2; 2) Allow opt-in to legacy-equivalent billing flag for a limited period; 3) Run telemetry job to generate per-model/seqlen factors. Long-term: incorporate conversion into billing pipeline and emit both raw and billing tokens to accounting.
deploybot: billing-service v3 deployed to staging with `billing_equiv` flag gated (canary tenants only).
Alice Chen: Next steps — create telemetry job (Carla + infra), billing pipeline PR (Ben), console mock for equiv display + banner copy (Dana), legal/finance sync about credits (I'll schedule). I'll open tickets and link here.
Dana Ortiz: I'll do a quick mock and ping legal. Draft copy: "We estimate your invoice will change by ~+18% with v2 due to tokenizer changes. Choose legacy-equivalent billing for 90 days to avoid sudden changes." Thoughts?
Ben Rao: Sounds good. I'll own the billing PR and add safe defaults (factor=1.0) and feature flag. Will wire header handling for debugging.
Carla Mendez: I'll start the telemetry job to compute median ratios and add dashboards (per-model, seqlen buckets, tenant sample) so product can see the distribution.
Alice Chen: Great — thanks. Let's reconvene after initial telemetry run and staging billing test. (+: Dana, Ben, Carla)
